Practitioners’ Circle

This is a three-day retreat for practitioners who want to lead groups with more confidence. Knowing your practice well is one thing, and leading a group is another.





The retreat will give wellness, bodymind and movement practitioners a place to practise group facilitation with each other. You will each lead a session in your own practice and then get feedback from the group, with a simple format for giving it. Along the way, you will experience other traditions from the inside and compare notes on what it takes to lead a group well.
We will look after the structure: daily opening and closing practices, a short check-in with you before you lead, and time to reflect together. That will leave you free to try new things as a facilitator, at the edge you choose.


Who it is for
Teachers, therapists and other practitioners. Adults (18+).


When
Tentatively May 2027. Three days.


Where
Germany.


Touch
Some sessions may involve touch between participants, such as a hand on the back or leaning into each other’s weight. This includes sessions that other participants lead. Touch is always optional: you can say no, or change your mind, at any time without giving a reason, and there is always a way to take part without it. Nothing in the retreat is sexual, and everyone stays clothed.


Included
Accommodation and food.


Language
English. Everyday English is enough.


Group
Around twelve participants.



Venue, exact dates and price to follow.


This retreat is not therapy or medical treatment. If you have a physical or mental health condition, please tell us before booking, so we can talk it through together.


Questions are welcome, about the programme, the place, cost, access or whether this is right for you. Write to us at hello@example.org, also if you would like to hear when the dates and price are set.

Moving Together

This is a three-day movement retreat for anyone. It brings together yoga, tantra and improvised movement, practised alone, in pairs and as a whole group.





What happens when a room full of people stops moving the way they think they should, and starts moving the way they actually feel? Some sessions will start from breath and awareness. Others will open space for play and creative expression, where you follow, lead, mirror and respond to the people around you, and find out what a group can do that no one can do alone.
Over the three days, there will be time to notice old habits, and to widen your attention from your own body to the group. No experience is needed, and there is no right way to do any of it.
We will share the group agreements before you book. Throughout, you are free to take part at your own pace — to sit out, or to watch.


Who it is for
Anyone curious about movement, connection and creativity, whether you have practised for years or are just beginning. Adults (18+).


When
Tentatively September 2027. Three days.


Where
Germany.

Some exercises will involve touch between participants, such as a hand on the back or leaning into each other’s weight. Touch is always optional: you can say no, or change your mind, at any time without giving a reason, and there is always a way to take part without it. Nothing in the retreat is sexual, and everyone stays clothed.

DS

DS is a yoga teacher and community activist.

title: About
text:
The name
Not knowing is usually treated as a gap, something to close as quickly as possible. We see it differently. While we do not yet know, we can still notice what is actually happening, rather than what we expected to happen.
This matters most with the body. Much of what is taught about it is less certain than it sounds, and even what is well established says little about what one person feels in one moment. A sensation, a breath or a meeting with another person can be met with a ready answer, or with attention. We would rather start from the question.
A garden does not grow from a plan alone. Things come up in their own time, and much of the work is watching and waiting. Notknowing Garden is a place to practise that, in a room and on the page.
